title: Personnel Schedule Record
body:
Overview

This record documents Personnel Schedule Record within the Operational Planning and Resource Allocation Database. Schedules personnel, equipment and resources against defined constraints. It gives the archive a reusable, checkable entry for one recurring task: the entry states what the task is, how it is done, and what result was measured or computed when the accompanying demo program ran. The record is written so a reader can follow it without any other document open, and so an AI can apply it to a new task of the same shape without guessing at missing steps. Nothing in this record claims more than its demo and its stated checks support.

How it works

The method in each record starts from constraints: people available, equipment available, time available, and the rules that limit how they combine. Allocation then assigns resources to tasks under those constraints and reports utilization, so over-allocation is visible instead of discovered during execution.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this entry is concrete. The demo program that accompanies this record ran at build time and produced a real, checkable result, beginning with: task A hours 6 people 2 running staff used 2. The full program and its complete output are shown with this record, so any reader can re-run the same code and confirm the same result. Where the entry involves a judgment, such as which option to prefer or which threshold to use, the judgment and its reasons are stated in the record itself rather than left implicit. Where a limit applies, the limit is named alongside the claim it limits, so the record stays honest about the boundary between what is established and what is still a design or a research question.

Use and ladder

A planner uses these records to build schedules that fit the resources that actually exist, to spot the bottleneck before it bites, and to reallocate cleanly when priorities change. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records handle the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, the record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. Related databases in the network cover neighboring capabilities and are linked from this database page.
demo_code:
# Personnel Schedule Record: allocate people to tasks under the staffing constraint.
tasks = [('task A', 6, 2), ('task B', 5, 3), ('task C', 8, 2), ('task D', 5, 1)]
staff_available = 6
used = 0
for name, hours, people in tasks:
    used += people
    print(name, "hours", hours, "people", people, "running staff used", used)
print("staff available:", staff_available)
print("staff required:", used)
print("within constraint:", used <= staff_available)
print("total task hours:", sum(h for _, h, _ in tasks))

task A hours 6 people 2 running staff used 2
task B hours 5 people 3 running staff used 5
task C hours 8 people 2 running staff used 7
task D hours 5 people 1 running staff used 8
staff available: 6
staff required: 8
within constraint: False
total task hours: 24
